--[[
	CurveSampling: reads Forge curve attributes and samples them into Part-Icles NumberSequences.
	Forge stores a curve with y falling from 1 to 0; alpha = 1 - ease(t).y is the forward progress.
	Forge's Speed_Curve time warp is baked into each graph's shape rather than Timescale, whose maths
	differs from Forge's dt scaling.

	API:
	  deserializeForgeCurve(data)  -> flat {x, y} control points, or nil
	  evalForgeCurveY(points, t), evalForgeAlpha(points, t), alphaAt(curveData, t, linearDefault)
	  seqLerpCurved(startVal, endVal, curveData, maxKeypoints, warpFn)  value blend along alpha
	  seqMotionFromCurve(distance, lifetime, curveData, samples, warpFn)  Speed graph from the motion curve's slope
	  buildSpeedWarp(...)  -> warpFn, effective lifetime
	  solveLifespan(...)   -> effective lifetime alone
	  evalBezier3D, sample3DBezier, sampleAdaptive3D  3D path sampling for BezierConverter
	  orientFromTangent_LookAt, orientFromTangent, unwrapAngles  path orientation helpers
]]

local CurveSampling = {}

-- Forge's curve when a *_Curve attribute is absent: an out-cubic, not linear. Anchors (0, 1) and
-- (1, 0) with handles (0.215, 0.39) and (0.355, 0).
local DEFAULT_BEZIER_POINTS = {
	{x = 0,     y = 1},
	{x = 0.215, y = 0.39},
	{x = 0.355, y = 0},
	{x = 1,     y = 0},
}

-- A *_Curve buffer holds 24 bytes per segment, six f32s (px, py, t1x, t1y, t2x, t2y); the last
-- segment is its anchor alone. Returns the flat point list, or nil.
function CurveSampling.deserializeForgeCurve(data)
	if not data then return nil end
	local buf
	if typeof(data) == "string" then buf = buffer.fromstring(data)
	elseif typeof(data) == "buffer" then buf = data
	else return nil end
	local len = buffer.len(buf)
	if len == 0 or len % 24 ~= 0 then return nil end
	local count = len / 24
	local points = {}
	for i = 0, count - 1 do
		local offset = i * 24
		points[#points + 1] = {x = buffer.readf32(buf, offset), y = buffer.readf32(buf, offset + 4)}
		if i ~= count - 1 then
			points[#points + 1] = {x = buffer.readf32(buf, offset + 8),  y = buffer.readf32(buf, offset + 12)}
			points[#points + 1] = {x = buffer.readf32(buf, offset + 16), y = buffer.readf32(buf, offset + 20)}
		end
	end
	return points
end

local function _cubicBez(a, b, c, d, s)
	local u = 1 - s
	return u * u * u * a + 3 * u * u * s * b + 3 * u * s * s * c + s * s * s * d
end

-- Eased y at time t: Newton steps find s where x(s) = t. Not clamped; the control points decide the range.
function CurveSampling.evalForgeCurveY(points, t)
	t = math.clamp(t, 0, 1)
	local segCount = math.floor((#points - 1) / 3)
	if segCount <= 0 then return t end
	local segIdx, segS = segCount, 1
	for k = 1, segCount do
		local startIdx = (k - 1) * 3 + 1
		local p0x = points[startIdx].x
		local p3x = points[startIdx + 3].x
		if t >= p0x and t <= p3x then
			segIdx = k
			segS = (p3x > p0x) and ((t - p0x) / (p3x - p0x)) or 0
			break
		end
	end
	local startIdx = (segIdx - 1) * 3 + 1
	local p0, p1, p2, p3 = points[startIdx], points[startIdx + 1], points[startIdx + 2], points[startIdx + 3]
	local s = segS
	for _ = 1, 6 do
		local x = _cubicBez(p0.x, p1.x, p2.x, p3.x, s)
		local dx = 3 * (1 - s) * (1 - s) * (p1.x - p0.x) + 6 * (1 - s) * s * (p2.x - p1.x) + 3 * s * s * (p3.x - p2.x)
		if dx == 0 then break end
		local ds = (x - t) / dx
		s = math.clamp(s - ds, 0, 1)
		if math.abs(ds) < 0.001 then break end
	end
	return _cubicBez(p0.y, p1.y, p2.y, p3.y, s)
end

-- Forward progress 1 - y at t; may leave [0, 1] for morph curves.
function CurveSampling.evalForgeAlpha(points, t)
	return 1 - CurveSampling.evalForgeCurveY(points, t)
end

-- Forge alpha at normalized t for a *_Curve attribute value. A missing curve falls back to
-- Forge's default out-cubic, or to linear when `linearDefault` is set (colour and easing curves).
function CurveSampling.alphaAt(curveData, t, linearDefault)
	local points = CurveSampling.deserializeForgeCurve(curveData)
	if not points then
		if linearDefault then return math.clamp(t, 0, 1) end
		points = DEFAULT_BEZIER_POINTS
	end
	return CurveSampling.evalForgeAlpha(points, t)
end

-- value(t) = lerp(startVal, endVal, alpha(warp(t))). A NumberSequence holds at most 20 keypoints,
-- so they sit at equal steps of accumulated change in alpha over 60 dense samples: a warp that packs
-- the change into a short window still gets keypoints there.
function CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(startVal, endVal, curveData, maxKeypoints, warpFn)
	local points = CurveSampling.deserializeForgeCurve(curveData) or DEFAULT_BEZIER_POINTS
	startVal = startVal or 0
	endVal = endVal or startVal
	maxKeypoints = math.min(maxKeypoints or 20, 20)

	local DENSE = 60
	local rawT = table.create(DENSE)
	local rawAlpha = table.create(DENSE)
	for i = 1, DENSE do
		local t = (i - 1) / (DENSE - 1)
		local sampleT = warpFn and math.clamp(warpFn(t), 0, 1) or t
		rawT[i] = t
		rawAlpha[i] = CurveSampling.evalForgeAlpha(points, sampleT)
	end

	local cumVar = table.create(DENSE)
	cumVar[1] = 0
	for i = 2, DENSE do
		cumVar[i] = cumVar[i - 1] + math.abs(rawAlpha[i] - rawAlpha[i - 1])
	end
	local totalVar = cumVar[DENSE]

	local kp = {}
	kp[1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, startVal + (endVal - startVal) * rawAlpha[1])
	if totalVar > 0 and maxKeypoints > 2 then
		local denom = maxKeypoints - 1
		for k = 2, maxKeypoints - 1 do
			local target = (k - 1) / denom * totalVar
			local idx = 2
			for i = 2, DENSE do
				if cumVar[i] >= target then idx = i; break end
			end
			local prev = cumVar[idx - 1]
			local span = cumVar[idx] - prev
			local frac = (span > 0) and (target - prev) / span or 0
			local tInterp = rawT[idx - 1] + (rawT[idx] - rawT[idx - 1]) * frac
			local alphaInterp = rawAlpha[idx - 1] + (rawAlpha[idx] - rawAlpha[idx - 1]) * frac
			-- NumberSequence rejects keypoints at the same time.
			if not kp[k - 1] or tInterp > kp[k - 1].Time + 0.0001 then
				kp[#kp + 1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(tInterp, startVal + (endVal - startVal) * alphaInterp)
			end
		end
	end
	kp[#kp + 1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, startVal + (endVal - startVal) * rawAlpha[DENSE])
	return NumberSequence.new(kp)
end

-- Speed(t) = d alpha(warp(t)) / dt x distance / lifetime, by finite differences, so the warp folds
-- into the slope. A negative slope moves backward, as Forge's Lerp past its ends does.
function CurveSampling.seqMotionFromCurve(distance, lifetime, curveData, samples, warpFn)
	samples = samples or 12
	if lifetime <= 0 or distance == 0 then return NumberSequence.new(0) end

	local points = CurveSampling.deserializeForgeCurve(curveData) or DEFAULT_BEZIER_POINTS

	local dt = 1 / (samples - 1)
	local alphas = table.create(samples)
	for i = 0, samples - 1 do
		local t = i * dt
		local sampleT = warpFn and math.clamp(warpFn(t), 0, 1) or t
		alphas[i + 1] = CurveSampling.evalForgeAlpha(points, sampleT)
	end

	local kp = {}
	for i = 1, samples do
		local t = (i - 1) * dt
		local dAlpha
		if i == 1 then
			dAlpha = (alphas[2] - alphas[1]) / dt
		elseif i == samples then
			dAlpha = (alphas[samples] - alphas[samples - 1]) / dt
		else
			dAlpha = (alphas[i + 1] - alphas[i - 1]) / (2 * dt)
		end
		local speed = dAlpha * distance / lifetime
		kp[i] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(t, speed)
	end
	return NumberSequence.new(kp)
end

-- Forge's speed at real time R: Speed_Start to Speed_End along Speed_Curve over Speed_Duration, then held.
local function _buildSpeedAt(speedStart, speedEnd, curveData, speedDuration)
	speedDuration = math.max(speedDuration or 0.1, 0.001)
	local points = CurveSampling.deserializeForgeCurve(curveData)
	local hasCurve = points and #points >= 4
	return function(realT)
		if realT >= speedDuration then return speedEnd end
		if realT <= 0 then return speedStart end
		local alpha
		if hasCurve then
			alpha = CurveSampling.evalForgeAlpha(points, realT / speedDuration)
		else
			alpha = realT / speedDuration
		end
		return speedStart + (speedEnd - speedStart) * alpha
	end, speedDuration
end

-- Midpoint-rule integral of speed over the ramp: area, running sums, step.
local function _integrateRamp(speedAt, speedDuration, steps)
	steps = steps or 64
	local rampSubdt = speedDuration / steps
	local rampCum = table.create(steps + 1)
	rampCum[1] = 0
	local sum = 0
	for i = 1, steps do
		sum = sum + speedAt((i - 0.5) * rampSubdt) * rampSubdt
		rampCum[i + 1] = sum
	end
	return sum, rampCum, rampSubdt
end

-- Forge's visible lifespan. A particle dies when its size tween's elapsed time reaches duration and
-- the speed tween (only when Speed_Start ~= Speed_End, lasting Speed_Duration) is over; a speed at or
-- below 0 then ends it at once.
--   1. constant speed above 0:       duration / speed
--   2. constant speed at or below 0: about 0
--   3. ramp ending above 0:          max(time to cover duration, Speed_Duration)
--   4. ramp ending at or below 0:    Speed_Duration
local function _solveTeff(speedAt, speedStart, speedEnd, speedDuration, duration)
	local rampArea, rampCum, rampSubdt = _integrateRamp(speedAt, speedDuration, 64)
	-- Regime 4.
	if speedStart ~= speedEnd and speedEnd <= 0 then
		return speedDuration, rampArea
	end
	-- Regime 2.
	if speedStart == speedEnd and speedEnd <= 0 then
		return 0.001, rampArea
	end
	local Tsize
	if rampArea >= duration then
		for i = 1, #rampCum - 1 do
			if rampCum[i + 1] >= duration then
				local prev = rampCum[i]
				local frac = (duration - prev) / (rampCum[i + 1] - prev)
				Tsize = (i - 1 + frac) * rampSubdt
				break
			end
		end
		Tsize = Tsize or speedDuration
	else
		-- speedEnd > 0 here: regimes 2 and 4 returned.
		Tsize = speedDuration + (duration - rampArea) / speedEnd
	end
	-- Regime 3.
	if speedStart ~= speedEnd and Tsize < speedDuration then
		return speedDuration, rampArea
	end
	-- Regime 1.
	return Tsize, rampArea
end

-- Effective lifespan alone, for each end of a Lifetime range (one ratio on the mean is off at the extremes).
function CurveSampling.solveLifespan(speedStart, speedEnd, curveData, speedDuration, duration)
	if speedStart == 1 and speedEnd == 1 and not curveData then return duration end
	if not duration or duration <= 0 then duration = 1 end
	local speedAt = _buildSpeedAt(speedStart, speedEnd, curveData, speedDuration)
	local Teff = _solveTeff(speedAt, speedStart, speedEnd, math.max(speedDuration or 0.1, 0.001), duration)
	return Teff
end

-- Returns warpFn, effective lifetime. Forge advances its size, transparency, rotation and motion
-- tweens by dt x speed; warpFn maps normalized life to their normalized progress, and the caller
-- sets Lifetime to the effective lifetime. Speed 1 with no curve gives the identity.
function CurveSampling.buildSpeedWarp(speedStart, speedEnd, curveData, speedDuration, duration)
	if speedStart == 1 and speedEnd == 1 and not curveData then
		return function(t) return t end, duration
	end
	if not duration or duration <= 0 then duration = 1 end
	speedDuration = math.max(speedDuration or 0.1, 0.001)

	local speedAt = _buildSpeedAt(speedStart, speedEnd, curveData, speedDuration)
	local Teff = _solveTeff(speedAt, speedStart, speedEnd, speedDuration, duration)

	-- elapsed is clamped to [0, duration] each step as in Forge, so a speed that turns negative stays
	-- in step with Forge's progress.
	local STEPS = 128
	local subdt = Teff / STEPS
	local lookup = table.create(STEPS + 1)
	lookup[1] = 0
	local elapsed = 0
	for i = 1, STEPS do
		elapsed = math.clamp(elapsed + speedAt((i - 0.5) * subdt) * subdt, 0, duration)
		lookup[i + 1] = elapsed
	end

	local warpFn = function(tNorm)
		if tNorm <= 0 then return 0 end
		if tNorm >= 1 then return math.clamp(lookup[STEPS + 1] / duration, 0, 1) end
		local idx = tNorm * STEPS
		local lo = math.floor(idx)
		local frac = idx - lo
		local loVal = lookup[lo + 1]
		local hiVal = lookup[lo + 2]
		return math.clamp((loVal + (hiVal - loVal) * frac) / duration, 0, 1)
	end

	return warpFn, Teff
end

-- 3D bezier paths, for BezierConverter.

-- Position at t in [0, 1] on a flat list of cubic segments {anchor, out handle, in handle, next anchor}.
function CurveSampling.evalBezier3D(points, t)
	local segCount = math.floor((#points - 1) / 3)
	if segCount <= 0 then return points[1] or Vector3.zero end
	t = math.clamp(t, 0, 1)
	local scaled = t * segCount
	local segIdx = math.min(math.floor(scaled), segCount - 1)
	local u = scaled - segIdx
	if t == 1 then segIdx = segCount - 1; u = 1 end
	local startIdx = segIdx * 3 + 1
	local p0 = points[startIdx]
	local p1 = points[startIdx + 1]
	local p2 = points[startIdx + 2]
	local p3 = points[startIdx + 3]
	local oneMinusU = 1 - u
	return p0 * (oneMinusU * oneMinusU * oneMinusU)
		+ p1 * (3 * oneMinusU * oneMinusU * u)
		+ p2 * (3 * oneMinusU * u * u)
		+ p3 * (u * u * u)
end

-- Arc length to parametric t, so a uniform sweep moves at uniform speed along the path. Returns arcToT(s).
local function _buildArcLookup(points, density)
	density = density or 64
	local cum = table.create(density + 1)
	cum[1] = 0
	local prev = CurveSampling.evalBezier3D(points, 0)
	for i = 1, density do
		local t = i / density
		local cur = CurveSampling.evalBezier3D(points, t)
		cum[i + 1] = cum[i] + (cur - prev).Magnitude
		prev = cur
	end
	local total = cum[density + 1]
	return function(s)
		if total <= 0 then return s end
		if s <= 0 then return 0 end
		if s >= 1 then return 1 end
		local target = s * total
		local lo, hi = 1, density + 1
		while lo + 1 < hi do
			local mid = math.floor((lo + hi) / 2)
			if cum[mid] <= target then lo = mid else hi = mid end
		end
		local span = cum[hi] - cum[lo]
		local frac = (span > 0) and ((target - cum[lo]) / span) or 0
		return ((lo - 1) + frac) / density
	end
end

-- positions[i], tangents[i] at `samples` uniform t, applied in Forge's order: arc length, then
-- Easing_Curve, then the speed warp. Tangents are central differences.
function CurveSampling.sample3DBezier(points, samples, easingCurveData, warpFn, arcSpace)
	samples = samples or 12
	local easingPoints = easingCurveData and CurveSampling.deserializeForgeCurve(easingCurveData)
	local arcToT = arcSpace and _buildArcLookup(points, 64) or nil
	local positions = table.create(samples)
	local tangents = table.create(samples)
	local dt = 1 / (samples - 1)

	for i = 1, samples do
		local t = (i - 1) * dt
		if warpFn then t = math.clamp(warpFn(t), 0, 1) end
		local alpha
		if easingPoints and #easingPoints >= 4 then
			alpha = math.clamp(CurveSampling.evalForgeAlpha(easingPoints, t), 0, 1)
		else
			alpha = t
		end
		if arcToT then alpha = arcToT(alpha) end
		positions[i] = CurveSampling.evalBezier3D(points, alpha)
	end

	for i = 1, samples do
		if i == 1 then
			tangents[i] = (positions[2] - positions[1]) / dt
		elseif i == samples then
			tangents[i] = (positions[samples] - positions[samples - 1]) / dt
		else
			tangents[i] = (positions[i + 1] - positions[i - 1]) / (2 * dt)
		end
	end

	return positions, tangents
end

-- CFrame whose LookVector (-Z) runs along `tangent`, as Forge's CFrame.lookAt does.
function CurveSampling.orientFromTangent_LookAt(tangent)
	if tangent.Magnitude < 0.001 then return CFrame.identity end
	return CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.zero, tangent.Unit)
end

-- Up to 20 keypoints at equal steps of accumulated tangent turn: dense at bends, sparse on
-- straights. Returns t values, positions, tangents.
function CurveSampling.sampleAdaptive3D(points, maxKeypoints, easingCurveData, warpFn, arcSpace)
	maxKeypoints = math.min(maxKeypoints or 20, 20)
	local DENSE = 60
	local positions, tangents = CurveSampling.sample3DBezier(points, DENSE, easingCurveData, warpFn, arcSpace)

	local cumVar = table.create(DENSE)
	cumVar[1] = 0
	for i = 2, DENSE do
		local prev = tangents[i - 1]
		local cur = tangents[i]
		local pm, cm = prev.Magnitude, cur.Magnitude
		local angleDelta = 0
		if pm > 1e-6 and cm > 1e-6 then
			local cosA = math.clamp((prev / pm):Dot(cur / cm), -1, 1)
			angleDelta = math.acos(cosA)
		end
		cumVar[i] = cumVar[i - 1] + angleDelta
	end
	local totalVar = cumVar[DENSE]

	-- First and last keypoints at 0 and 1; NumberSequence rejects equal times.
	local out_t = { 0 }
	local out_positions = { positions[1] }
	local out_tangents = { tangents[1] }

	if totalVar > 1e-6 and maxKeypoints > 2 then
		local denom = maxKeypoints - 1
		for k = 2, maxKeypoints - 1 do
			local target = (k - 1) / denom * totalVar
			local idx = 2
			for i = 2, DENSE do
				if cumVar[i] >= target then idx = i; break end
			end
			local prev = cumVar[idx - 1]
			local span = cumVar[idx] - prev
			local frac = (span > 0) and (target - prev) / span or 0
			local denseT_lo = (idx - 2) / (DENSE - 1)
			local denseT_hi = (idx - 1) / (DENSE - 1)
			local tInterp = denseT_lo + (denseT_hi - denseT_lo) * frac
			local posInterp = positions[idx - 1]:Lerp(positions[idx], frac)
			local tanInterp = tangents[idx - 1]:Lerp(tangents[idx], frac)
			if tInterp > out_t[#out_t] + 0.0001 then
				out_t[#out_t + 1] = tInterp
				out_positions[#out_positions + 1] = posInterp
				out_tangents[#out_tangents + 1] = tanInterp
			end
		end
	end

	if 1 > out_t[#out_t] + 0.0001 then
		out_t[#out_t + 1] = 1
		out_positions[#out_positions + 1] = positions[DENSE]
		out_tangents[#out_tangents + 1] = tangents[DENSE]
	end

	return out_t, out_positions, out_tangents
end

-- CFrame whose +Y runs along `tangent`; identity for a zero tangent, world X as up near world Y.
function CurveSampling.orientFromTangent(tangent)
	if tangent.Magnitude < 0.001 then return CFrame.identity end
	local t = tangent.Unit
	local up = Vector3.yAxis
	if math.abs(t:Dot(up)) > 0.99 then up = Vector3.xAxis end
	local right = up:Cross(t).Unit
	return CFrame.fromMatrix(Vector3.zero, right, t)
end

-- Removes jumps above pi between neighbours by shifting the rest by 2 pi. Mutates and returns.
function CurveSampling.unwrapAngles(values)
	local offset = 0
	for i = 2, #values do
		local diff = (values[i] + offset) - values[i - 1]
		if diff > math.pi then
			offset = offset - 2 * math.pi
		elseif diff < -math.pi then
			offset = offset + 2 * math.pi
		end
		values[i] = values[i] + offset
	end
	return values
end

return CurveSampling

--[[
	EffectConverters: rewrites each Forge effect in the cloned output tree into its Part-Icles
	equivalent, in place. Mesh, beam, particle, trail, spin and screen live here; bezier, lightning,
	sound, camera shake and shockwave dispatch to their own modules; tweeners are skipped.

	Mesh: Start becomes the emitter and End the morph target. Forge's curves drive the matching graphs,
	and the Speed_Curve time warp is baked into every graph (CurveSampling.buildSpeedWarp).
	Exact conversions count in successCount; shockwaves and screen parts in approxCount with a warning.
	A static spin Model (no rotation, scale change or position sync) stays a plain container.

	API:
	  rewriteInPlace(ctx, node, kind, report)  the walker's dispatcher (init.luau)
	  convertMesh, convertBeam, convertBeamInPlace, convertParticle, convertTrail, convertSpin, convertScreen
	  convertShockwavePart, convertShockwaveContainer  re-exported from ShockwaveConverter
]]

local Helpers = require(script.Parent.Helpers)
local CurveSampling = require(script.Parent.CurveSampling)
local MeshAppearance = require(script.Parent.MeshAppearance)
local EventsSchema = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.EventsSchema)

local EffectConverters = {}

-- Returns srcAtt's counterpart on a copy of its part inside `host` (one copy per part, kept in
-- parentMirrors), or srcAtt itself when it is already inside host. The copy keeps only the part's
-- attachments, emptied: it marks where the ends are. Declared above convertMesh, which calls it.
local function mirrorAttachmentInto(srcAtt, host, parentMirrors)
	if not srcAtt then return nil end
	local srcParent = srcAtt.Parent
	if not (srcParent and srcParent:IsA("BasePart")) then return nil end
	if srcParent:IsDescendantOf(host) then return srcAtt end
	local mirror = parentMirrors[srcParent]
	if not mirror then
		mirror = srcParent:Clone()
		for _, c in ipairs(mirror:GetChildren()) do
			if c:IsA("Attachment") then
				for _, held in ipairs(c:GetChildren()) do held:Destroy() end
			else
				c:Destroy()
			end
		end
		mirror.Anchored = true
		mirror.CanCollide = false
		mirror.CanQuery = false
		mirror.CanTouch = false
		mirror.Transparency = 1
		mirror.Parent = host
		parentMirrors[srcParent] = mirror
	end
	return mirror:FindFirstChild(srcAtt.Name)
end


-- Rewrites a Forge mesh wrapper Model: an emitter made from Start replaces Start and End, other
-- children stay, and the wrapper's Forge attributes go.
function EffectConverters.convertMesh(ctx, sourceModel, report)
	local startPart = sourceModel:FindFirstChild("Start")
	local endPart = sourceModel:FindFirstChild("End")
	if not (startPart and endPart and startPart:IsA("BasePart") and endPart:IsA("BasePart")) then
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = "Mesh effect '" .. sourceModel:GetFullName() .. "' missing Start or End child; skipped."
		report.skippedCount += 1
		return
	end

	-- Named after the bundle, not "Start".
	local clone = startPart:Clone()
	clone.Name = sourceModel.Name .. "_Emitter"
	clone.Parent = sourceModel
	clone.Anchored = true
	clone.CanCollide = false
	clone.CanQuery = false
	clone.CanTouch = false

	-- Effect children and Attachments are detached before Transform: its strip would destroy the
	-- effects, and Attachments copied into the RenderTemplate would leave Trails pointing outside it,
	-- so every emitted copy's Trail would share the source's Attachments.
	local survivors = {}
	local nestedForgeBeams = {}
	for _, child in ipairs(clone:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Beam") then
			nestedForgeBeams[#nestedForgeBeams + 1] = child
			child.Parent = nil
		elseif child:IsA("ParticleEmitter") or child:IsA("Trail")
			or child:IsA("Sound") or child:IsA("BasePart") or child:IsA("Model")
			or child:IsA("Light") or child:IsA("Highlight")
			or child:IsA("Attachment") then
			survivors[#survivors + 1] = child
			child.Parent = nil
		end
	end

	-- Stale Transformed / IsEmitter markers would make stripAllForge skip the clone and Transform return early.
	Helpers.clearPartIclesMarkers(clone)

	-- The maths reads the untouched originals, so the clone drops every attribute and tag.
	Helpers.stripAllForge(clone)

	local ok, err = pcall(function() ctx.Part:Transform(clone) end)
	if not ok then
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format("Transform errored on '%s': %s", sourceModel.Name, tostring(err))
		report.skippedCount += 1
		clone:Destroy()
		return
	end
	local cfgCheck = clone:FindFirstChild("PartIcleProperties")
	if not cfgCheck then
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format("'%s' (%s) was not recognized as a Transformable type  -  PartIcleProperties not created. Conversion skipped.", sourceModel.Name, clone.ClassName)
		report.skippedCount += 1
		clone:Destroy()
		return
	end

	-- Back into the RenderTemplate; Trail refs still point at the moved Attachments. Nested Beams usually
	-- end on parts outside the clone, so their ends are mirrored in, or they break when the source goes.
	local rt = clone:FindFirstChild("RenderTemplate")
	if rt then
		for _, p in ipairs(survivors) do
			-- Keeps the nested-emit attributes: without EmitDuration a Trail is never enabled after emit.
			Helpers.stripPreservingNestedEmit(p)
			p.Parent = rt
		end
		local nestedParentMirrors = {}
		for _, beam in ipairs(nestedForgeBeams) do
			beam.Parent = rt
			local newA0 = mirrorAttachmentInto(beam.Attachment0, rt, nestedParentMirrors)
			local newA1 = mirrorAttachmentInto(beam.Attachment1, rt, nestedParentMirrors)
			if newA0 then beam.Attachment0 = newA0 end
			if newA1 then beam.Attachment1 = newA1 end
			EffectConverters.convertBeamInPlace(ctx, beam, report)
		end
		if rt:IsA("BasePart") and startPart:IsA("BasePart") and startPart.CastShadow then
			pcall(function() rt.CastShadow = true end)
		end
	end

	-- Transform took the mesh, decals and nested effects into the RenderTemplate; the rest goes.
	local _KEEP = {
		PartIcleProperties = true, RenderTemplate = true,
		EmitParent = true, Link = true, AccelTarget = true, Dir = true, ShapePart = true,
		MeshFlipbooks = true, MeshFrames = true, BeamFlipbooks = true, ImageFlipbooks = true, GraphBlender = true,
	}
	for _, child in ipairs(clone:GetChildren()) do
		if not _KEEP[child.Name] then child:Destroy() end
	end

	local TR = ctx.TypeRegistry
	local lifetime = Helpers.readDuration(sourceModel)
	local meanLifetime = (lifetime.Min + lifetime.Max) / 2
	if meanLifetime <= 0 then meanLifetime = 1 end

	TR.write(clone, "Lifetime", lifetime)
	local rate = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "Rate")
	if rate then TR.write(clone, "Rate", rate) end

	local speedStartMult = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "Speed_Start", 1)
	local speedEndMult = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "Speed_End", 1)
	local speedCurve = sourceModel:GetAttribute("Speed_Curve")
	local speedDuration = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "Speed_Duration", 0.1)

	-- Forge's effective lifespan, for the mean and for each end of the Lifetime range.
	local warpFn, effectiveLifespanMean = CurveSampling.buildSpeedWarp(
		speedStartMult, speedEndMult, speedCurve, speedDuration, meanLifetime
	)
	local teffMin = CurveSampling.solveLifespan(speedStartMult, speedEndMult, speedCurve, speedDuration, lifetime.Min)
	local teffMax = CurveSampling.solveLifespan(speedStartMult, speedEndMult, speedCurve, speedDuration, lifetime.Max)
	if teffMin ~= lifetime.Min or teffMax ~= lifetime.Max then
		TR.write(clone, "Lifetime", NumberRange.new(teffMin, teffMax))
	end

	-- MinInitRot / MaxInitRot and SpreadAngle both set the initial pose: X and Y widen by the spread;
	-- Forge does not use SpreadAngle.Z.
	local minRot = sourceModel:GetAttribute("MinInitRot") or Vector3.zero
	local maxRot = sourceModel:GetAttribute("MaxInitRot") or Vector3.zero
	local spread = sourceModel:GetAttribute("SpreadAngle") or Vector3.zero
	if typeof(minRot) ~= "Vector3" then minRot = Vector3.zero end
	if typeof(maxRot) ~= "Vector3" then maxRot = Vector3.zero end
	if typeof(spread) ~= "Vector3" then spread = Vector3.zero end
	-- Forge applies the rolled rotation twice unless RotAroundOrigin moves one in front of the travel
	-- offset, so a mesh that spins in place shows double the angle.
	local rotAroundOrigin = sourceModel:GetAttribute("RotAroundOrigin") == true
	local selfRotFactor = rotAroundOrigin and 1 or 2

	-- Rotation is a Start -> End CFrame tween (RotMode OverLife) or Part_RotSpeed spin (RotMode Speed);
	-- RotMode holds one, and the spin wins when set. Forge's RotSpeed is radians per second, tweened
	-- over the whole life; Part-Icles' is degrees per second.
	local rotCurve = sourceModel:GetAttribute("Part_RotSpeed_Curve")
	local rotSpeedStartRange = Helpers.range(sourceModel, "Part_RotSpeed_Start", 0, 0)
	local rotSpeedEndRange = Helpers.range(sourceModel, "Part_RotSpeed_End", 0, 0)
	-- A range symmetric around 0 (spin either way) has a mean of 0: its larger end keeps the rate, and
	-- the sign comes from the initial rotation.
	local function _repRate(range)
		local mid = (range.Min + range.Max) * 0.5
		if math.abs(mid) < 1e-6 then return math.max(math.abs(range.Min), math.abs(range.Max)) end
		return mid
	end
	local rotSpeedMeanStart = _repRate(rotSpeedStartRange)
	local rotSpeedMeanEnd = _repRate(rotSpeedEndRange)
	-- Forge spins an axis only when its rolled initial rotation is non-zero (initRot:Sign()).
	-- A range that spans zero rolls either direction per emit; the positive one is kept.
	local function axisSign(minValue, maxValue)
		if minValue == 0 and maxValue == 0 then return 0 end
		if (minValue + maxValue) * 0.5 < 0 then return -1 end
		return 1
	end
	local sX = axisSign(minRot.X, maxRot.X)
	local sY = axisSign(minRot.Y, maxRot.Y)
	local sZ = axisSign(minRot.Z, maxRot.Z)
	local spinsAnyAxis = sX ~= 0 or sY ~= 0 or sZ ~= 0
	local hasRotSpeed = spinsAnyAxis and (math.abs(rotSpeedMeanStart) > 1e-6 or math.abs(rotSpeedMeanEnd) > 1e-6)

	if hasRotSpeed then
		local RAD_TO_DEG = math.deg(1)
		local degStart = rotSpeedMeanStart * RAD_TO_DEG * selfRotFactor
		local degEnd = rotSpeedMeanEnd * RAD_TO_DEG * selfRotFactor

		-- Linear over the life; Part_RotSpeed_Curve is not applied.
		TR.write(clone, "RotMode", "Speed")
		TR.write(clone, "RotSpeedX", Helpers.seq2(degStart * sX, degEnd * sX))
		TR.write(clone, "RotSpeedY", Helpers.seq2(degStart * sY, degEnd * sY))
		TR.write(clone, "RotSpeedZ", Helpers.seq2(degStart * sZ, degEnd * sZ))
	else
		-- OverLife adds to the spawn rotation (Start's), so the graphs run from 0 to the Start -> End delta.
		-- tweenableEulerDeg avoids the YXZ alias of single-axis turns past 90 degrees.
		local deltaRot = (startPart.CFrame:Inverse() * endPart.CFrame).Rotation
		local dRX, dRY, dRZ = Helpers.tweenableEulerDeg(deltaRot)
		TR.write(clone, "RotSpeedX", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(0, dRX, rotCurve, nil, warpFn))
		TR.write(clone, "RotSpeedY", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(0, dRY, rotCurve, nil, warpFn))
		TR.write(clone, "RotSpeedZ", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(0, dRZ, rotCurve, nil, warpFn))
	end
	local rotMinX = math.min(minRot.X, maxRot.X) * selfRotFactor - spread.X
	local rotMaxX = math.max(minRot.X, maxRot.X) * selfRotFactor + spread.X
	local rotMinY = math.min(minRot.Y, maxRot.Y) * selfRotFactor - spread.Y
	local rotMaxY = math.max(minRot.Y, maxRot.Y) * selfRotFactor + spread.Y
	local rotMinZ = math.min(minRot.Z, maxRot.Z) * selfRotFactor
	local rotMaxZ = math.max(minRot.Z, maxRot.Z) * selfRotFactor
	if rotMinX ~= 0 or rotMaxX ~= 0 then TR.write(clone, "RotX", NumberRange.new(rotMinX, rotMaxX)) end
	if rotMinY ~= 0 or rotMaxY ~= 0 then TR.write(clone, "RotY", NumberRange.new(rotMinY, rotMaxY)) end
	if rotMinZ ~= 0 or rotMaxZ ~= 0 then TR.write(clone, "RotZ", NumberRange.new(rotMinZ, rotMaxZ)) end

	-- Forge authors the visible scale on the SpecialMesh; Size is only the hull.
	local startMesh = startPart:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
	local endMesh = endPart:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
	local startSize = (startMesh and startMesh.Scale) or startPart.Size
	local endSize = (endMesh and endMesh.Scale) or endPart.Size
	-- The Size graphs drive SpecialMesh.Scale when both ends carry one, which Forge tweens on
	-- Mesh_Scale_Curve; a bare part tweens Size on Part_Size_Curve.
	local sizeCurve = sourceModel:GetAttribute("Part_Size_Curve")
	if startMesh and endMesh then
		sizeCurve = sourceModel:GetAttribute("Mesh_Scale_Curve") or sizeCurve
	end
	TR.write(clone, "SizeX", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(startSize.X, endSize.X, sizeCurve, nil, warpFn))
	TR.write(clone, "SizeY", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(startSize.Y, endSize.Y, sizeCurve, nil, warpFn))
	TR.write(clone, "SizeZ", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(startSize.Z, endSize.Z, sizeCurve, nil, warpFn))

	-- Forge lerps Start -> End along Part_CFrame_Curve; each PosOffset axis runs from 0 to the delta in
	-- Start's frame.
	local startCF = startPart.CFrame
	local endCF = endPart.CFrame
	local deltaLocal = (startCF:Inverse() * endCF).Position
	local cfCurve = sourceModel:GetAttribute("Part_CFrame_Curve")
	TR.write(clone, "PosOffsetX", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(0, deltaLocal.X, cfCurve, nil, warpFn))
	TR.write(clone, "PosOffsetY", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(0, deltaLocal.Y, cfCurve, nil, warpFn))
	TR.write(clone, "PosOffsetZ", CurveSampling.seqLerpCurved(0, deltaLocal.Z, cfCurve, nil, warpFn))
	-- Forge turns the path by the per-emit SpreadAngle and, with RotAroundOrigin, by the rolled
	-- rotation: "Local" follows each particle's roll. A plain initial rotation spins the mesh in place,
	-- so the path keeps the emitter's frame ("RigidLocal").
	local pathFollowsRoll = rotAroundOrigin or spread ~= Vector3.zero
	TR.write(clone, "DisplacementMode", pathFollowsRoll and "Local" or "RigidLocal")

	MeshAppearance.apply(ctx, sourceModel, startPart, endPart, clone, warpFn)

	-- Forge holds the finished mesh for DestroyDelay seconds before removing it.
	local destroyDelay = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "DestroyDelay", 0)
	if typeof(destroyDelay) == "number" and destroyDelay > 0 then
		TR.write(clone, "PartLife", destroyDelay)
	end

	local emitCount = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "EmitCount", 1)
	local emitDelay = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "EmitDelay", 0)
	local emitDur = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "EmitDuration", 0)
	clone:SetAttribute("EmitCount", emitCount)
	clone:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", emitDelay)
	clone:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", emitDur)

	-- Forge keeps the mesh alive for its longest flipbook pass, so a longer pass extends Lifetime.
	local frameCount, longestPass = MeshAppearance.applyFlipbooks(startPart, clone)
	if frameCount > 0 then
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format("Imported %d flipbook frames for '%s'.", frameCount, sourceModel.Name)
		if longestPass > teffMax then
			TR.write(clone, "Lifetime", NumberRange.new(longestPass))
		end
	end

	-- Start / End were only inputs; the wrapper's other children stay.
	startPart:Destroy()
	endPart:Destroy()

	-- stripAllForge skips the Transformed emitter, so its attributes survive.
	Helpers.stripAllForge(sourceModel)

	report.successCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.mesh = (report.mappedTypes.mesh or 0) + 1
end


-- Reads the beam's Forge attributes, strips them, Transforms the beam and writes its graphs. The
-- caller parents it and fixes its attachments.
function EffectConverters.convertBeamInPlace(ctx, beam, report)
	-- Read before the strip.
	local function _meanRange(v) return typeof(v) == "NumberRange" and ((v.Min + v.Max) / 2) or v end
	local widthData = {}
	for _, prop in ipairs({"Width0", "Width1", "CurveSize0", "CurveSize1"}) do
		widthData[prop] = {
			s = _meanRange(beam:GetAttribute(prop .. "_Start")),
			e = _meanRange(beam:GetAttribute(prop .. "_End")),
		}
	end
	local tStart = _meanRange(beam:GetAttribute("Transparency_Scale_Start")) or 0
	local tEnd = _meanRange(beam:GetAttribute("Transparency_Scale_End")) or tStart
	local txStart = _meanRange(beam:GetAttribute("Speed_Texture_Start"))
	local txEnd = txStart and (_meanRange(beam:GetAttribute("Speed_Texture_End")) or txStart) or nil
	local emitDelay = Helpers.attr(beam, "EmitDelay", 0)
	local emitDuration = Helpers.attr(beam, "EmitDuration", 0)
	local durHost = beam.Parent and beam.Parent:IsA("Model") and beam.Parent or beam
	local lifetime = Helpers.readDuration(durHost)

	Helpers.clearPartIclesMarkers(beam)
	Helpers.stripAllForge(beam)
	ctx.Part:Transform(beam)

	local TR = ctx.TypeRegistry
	TR.write(beam, "Lifetime", lifetime)
	for _, prop in ipairs({"Width0", "Width1", "CurveSize0", "CurveSize1"}) do
		local s = widthData[prop].s
		local e = widthData[prop].e or s
		if s ~= nil then TR.write(beam, prop, Helpers.seq2(s, e)) end
	end
	if txStart then TR.write(beam, "TextureSpeed", Helpers.seq2(txStart, txEnd)) end

	-- Beam transparency lives in GraphBlender states: state 1 (from Transform) takes the start scale,
	-- and a state 2 at Time 1 the end scale when it differs.
	local authoredTransparency = beam.Transparency
	local gb = beam:FindFirstChild("GraphBlender")
	if gb then
		local state1 = gb:FindFirstChild("1")
		if state1 then
			state1:SetAttribute("Transparency", Helpers.applyTransparencyScale(authoredTransparency, tStart))
		end
		if math.abs(tStart - tEnd) > 1e-3 then
			local state2 = Instance.new("Configuration")
			state2.Name = "2"
			state2:SetAttribute("Time", 1)
			state2:SetAttribute("Transparency", Helpers.applyTransparencyScale(authoredTransparency, tEnd))
			state2:SetAttribute("Color", beam.Color)
			state2:SetAttribute("_AutoTime", true)
			state2.Parent = gb
		end
	end

	beam:SetAttribute("EmitCount", 1)
	beam:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", emitDelay)
	beam:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", emitDuration)

	report.successCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.beam = (report.mappedTypes.beam or 0) + 1
end

-- Rewrites a cloned Forge Beam in place, mirroring ends that lie outside the converted tree.
function EffectConverters.convertBeam(ctx, beam, report)
	local host = beam.Parent or workspace
	local parentMirrors = {}
	-- An end needs a copy of its part only outside the converted tree (ctx.convertRoot) and off the
	-- beam's own part. Copying the beam's own part into its attachment would nest the part, beams and
	-- all, once per beam: 2^n copies, enough to stop Studio.
	local function outside(attachment)
		if not attachment then
			return false
		end
		if ctx.convertRoot and attachment:IsDescendantOf(ctx.convertRoot) then
			return false
		end
		local part = attachment.Parent
		return not (part == host or host:IsDescendantOf(part))
	end
	local newA0 = outside(beam.Attachment0) and mirrorAttachmentInto(beam.Attachment0, host, parentMirrors)
	local newA1 = outside(beam.Attachment1) and mirrorAttachmentInto(beam.Attachment1, host, parentMirrors)
	if newA0 then beam.Attachment0 = newA0 end
	if newA1 then beam.Attachment1 = newA1 end
	EffectConverters.convertBeamInPlace(ctx, beam, report)
end


-- Swaps a raw ParticleEmitter's Forge attributes for the three nested-emit attributes.
function EffectConverters.convertParticle(_ctx, pe, report)
	local emitCount = Helpers.attr(pe, "EmitCount", 1)
	local emitDelay = Helpers.attr(pe, "EmitDelay", 0)
	local emitDuration = Helpers.attr(pe, "EmitDuration", 0)

	Helpers.stripAllForge(pe)

	pe:SetAttribute("EmitCount", emitCount)
	pe:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", emitDelay)
	pe:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", emitDuration)

	report.successCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.particle = (report.mappedTypes.particle or 0) + 1
end


-- Same for a Trail. EmitDuration defaults to infinite so the Trail stays on through each emit until
-- the particle ends.
function EffectConverters.convertTrail(_ctx, trail, report)
	local emitDelay = Helpers.attr(trail, "EmitDelay", 0)
	local emitDuration = Helpers.attr(trail, "EmitDuration", math.huge)

	Helpers.stripAllForge(trail)

	trail:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", emitDelay)
	trail:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", emitDuration)
	trail.Enabled = false
	report.successCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.trail = (report.mappedTypes.trail or 0) + 1
end


-- The spin Model itself is transformed as a Model. Nested emitters converted earlier stay inside
-- (stripAllForge skips Transformed subtrees) and fire with each emit.
function EffectConverters.convertSpin(ctx, sourceModel, report)
	if not sourceModel.PrimaryPart then
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = "Spin model '" .. sourceModel.Name .. "' has no PrimaryPart; skipped."
		report.skippedCount += 1
		return
	end

	local dur = NumberRange.new(Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "SpinDuration", 1))
	local spinRot = sourceModel:GetAttribute("SpinRotation")
	local sStart = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "Scale_Start", 1)
	local sEnd = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "Scale_End", sStart)
	local emitCount = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "EmitCount", 1)
	local emitDelay = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "EmitDelay", 0)
	local emitDuration = Helpers.attr(sourceModel, "EmitDuration", 0)

	-- Stale markers would make stripAllForge skip and Transform return early.
	Helpers.clearPartIclesMarkers(sourceModel)

	Helpers.stripAllForge(sourceModel)
	ctx.Part:Transform(sourceModel)

	local TR = ctx.TypeRegistry
	TR.write(sourceModel, "Lifetime", dur)

	if typeof(spinRot) == "Vector3" then
		local meanDur = (dur.Min + dur.Max) / 2
		local denom = meanDur > 0 and meanDur or 1
		TR.write(sourceModel, "RotSpeedX", Helpers.seq2(spinRot.X / denom, spinRot.X / denom))
		TR.write(sourceModel, "RotSpeedY", Helpers.seq2(spinRot.Y / denom, spinRot.Y / denom))
		TR.write(sourceModel, "RotSpeedZ", Helpers.seq2(spinRot.Z / denom, spinRot.Z / denom))
	end

	TR.write(sourceModel, "SizeX", Helpers.seq2(sStart, sEnd))
	TR.write(sourceModel, "SizeY", Helpers.seq2(sStart, sEnd))
	TR.write(sourceModel, "SizeZ", Helpers.seq2(sStart, sEnd))

	sourceModel:SetAttribute("EmitCount", emitCount)
	sourceModel:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", emitDelay)
	sourceModel:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", emitDuration)

	report.successCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.spin = (report.mappedTypes.spin or 0) + 1
end

EffectConverters.convertShockwaveContainer = ShockwaveConverter.convertShockwaveContainer

-- The walker's dispatcher (init.luau). Wrappers (mesh, spin) keep their Model; attachment kinds
-- (bezier, lightning, shockwave_attachment) replace the attachment with an emitter Part; leaves are
-- rewritten in place.
function EffectConverters.rewriteInPlace(ctx, node, kind, report)
	if kind == "mesh"     then EffectConverters.convertMesh(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "spin"     then EffectConverters.convertSpin(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "static_model" then Helpers.stripOwnForge(node); return end
	if kind == "particle" then EffectConverters.convertParticle(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "trail"    then EffectConverters.convertTrail(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "sound"    then SoundConverter.convert(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "camera_shake" then CameraShakeConverter.convert(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "screen"   then EffectConverters.convertScreen(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "beam"     then EffectConverters.convertBeam(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "bezier"   then BezierConverter.convert(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "lightning" then LightningConverter.convert(ctx, node, report); return end
	if kind == "shockwave_attachment" then
		ShockwaveConverter.rewriteShockwave(ctx, node, nil, report); return
	end
	if kind == "skip:lightning" or kind == "skip:camera_shake" or kind == "skip:tweener" then
		local label = kind:sub(6)
		report.skippedCount += 1
		report.mappedTypes.skipped[label] = (report.mappedTypes.skipped[label] or 0) + 1
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format(
			"Skipped %s effect '%s' (not supported by Part-Icles V2).", label, node.Name)
		-- The skipped node goes so its Forge tag does not linger in the output.
		node:Destroy()
		return
	end
end


-- A screen-space part becomes a plain world-space Part.
function EffectConverters.convertScreen(_ctx, part, report)
	Helpers.stripAllForge(part)
	part.Anchored = true
	report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = "Screen-space part '" .. part.Name .. "' converted as worldspace Part. Camera-relative behavior is not preserved; reauthor in Studio if needed."
	report.approxCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.screen = (report.mappedTypes.screen or 0) + 1
end

return EffectConverters

--[[
	Helpers: shared utilities of the Forge converter. Reads and writes instances only.

	API:
	  TAGS, classify(inst) -> kind or nil, isStaticSpin(model), uniqueChildName(container, name)
	  attr, range, readDuration  attribute readers with defaults
	  seq2, lateRampSeq, earlyRampSeq, threeStageSeq, colorSeq2, clampColor, applyTransparencyScale
	  closestEmissionDirection, eulerDegYXZ, axisAngle, tweenableEulerDeg
	  deserializeFlipbook(data) -> asset ids
	  clearPartIclesMarkers, stripOwnForge, stripAllForge, stripPreservingNestedEmit
	  wireEmitTarget(ctx, clone, source, report, srcChildName, eventName, outFolderName, srcLabel) -> armed
]]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local EventsSchema = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.EventsSchema)
local AtRest = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.AtRest)

local Helpers = {}

-- Forge's CollectionService tag names.
Helpers.TAGS = {
	BEZIER = "BezierParticle",
	LIGHTNING = "LightningBolt",
	SCREENSHAKE = "CameraShake",
	TWEENER = "AttributeTweener",
	SHOCKWAVE = "Shockwave",
	CONSTANT = "ConstantVFX",
}

-- `name`, or `name_2`, `name_3` ... when a sibling already has it.
function Helpers.uniqueChildName(container, name)
	if not container:FindFirstChild(name) then return name end
	local i = 2
	while container:FindFirstChild(name .. "_" .. i) do i += 1 end
	return name .. "_" .. i
end

-- A Model with no spin, scale change or position sync does nothing when Forge emits it, so it
-- converts as a plain container.
function Helpers.isStaticSpin(model)
	local rotation = model:GetAttribute("SpinRotation")
	local spins = typeof(rotation) == "Vector3" and rotation ~= Vector3.zero
	local scales = Helpers.attr(model, "Scale_Start", 1) ~= 1 or Helpers.attr(model, "Scale_End", 1) ~= 1
	local syncs = model:GetAttribute("SyncPosition") == true
	return not (spins or scales or syncs)
end

-- The converter's effect kind for a Forge instance, or nil when the walker should keep descending.
function Helpers.classify(inst)
	if inst:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then return "particle" end
	if inst:IsA("Beam") then return "beam" end
	if inst:IsA("Trail") then return "trail" end
	if inst:IsA("Sound") then return "sound" end
	if inst:IsA("Attachment") then
		if CollectionService:HasTag(inst, Helpers.TAGS.BEZIER) then return "bezier" end
		if CollectionService:HasTag(inst, Helpers.TAGS.SHOCKWAVE) then return "shockwave_attachment" end
	end
	if CollectionService:HasTag(inst, Helpers.TAGS.LIGHTNING) then
		return inst:IsA("Attachment") and "lightning" or "skip:lightning"
	end
	if CollectionService:HasTag(inst, Helpers.TAGS.SCREENSHAKE) then
		return inst:IsA("RayValue") and "camera_shake" or "skip:camera_shake"
	end
	if CollectionService:HasTag(inst, Helpers.TAGS.TWEENER) then return "skip:tweener" end
	if inst:IsA("Model") then
		local s = inst:FindFirstChild("Start")
		local e = inst:FindFirstChild("End")
		if s and e and s:IsA("BasePart") and e:IsA("BasePart") then return "mesh" end
		if inst:GetAttribute("SpinRotation") ~= nil then
			if Helpers.isStaticSpin(inst) then return "static_model" end
			return "spin"
		end
	end
	if inst:IsA("BasePart") and inst:GetAttribute("PartDistance") ~= nil then return "screen" end
	return nil
end

function Helpers.attr(inst, name, default)
	local v = inst:GetAttribute(name)
	if v == nil then return default end
	return v
end

-- Forge NumberRange attributes sometimes come as plain numbers.
function Helpers.range(inst, name, defaultMin, defaultMax)
	local v = inst:GetAttribute(name)
	if typeof(v) == "NumberRange" then return v end
	if typeof(v) == "number" then return NumberRange.new(v) end
	return NumberRange.new(defaultMin or 0, defaultMax or defaultMin or 0)
end

function Helpers.seq2(startVal, endVal)
	startVal = startVal or 0
	endVal = endVal or startVal
	return NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, startVal),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, endVal),
	})
end

-- Holds startVal until holdEnd, then ramps to endVal at 1 (Forge's end-of-life fades).
function Helpers.lateRampSeq(startVal, endVal, holdEnd)
	holdEnd = math.clamp(holdEnd, 0, 1)
	if holdEnd <= 0 then return Helpers.seq2(startVal, endVal) end
	if holdEnd >= 1 then return NumberSequence.new(startVal) end
	return NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, startVal),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(holdEnd, startVal),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, endVal),
	})
end

-- Forge's beam transparency scale on each keypoint: above 1 moves toward transparent
-- (v + (1 - v) * (s - 1)), below 1 toward opaque (v * s). Returns a new sequence.
function Helpers.applyTransparencyScale(seq, tscale)
	if not seq or math.abs(tscale - 1) < 1e-3 then return seq end
	local offset = tscale > 1 and (tscale - 1) or (1 - tscale)
	local kps = {}
	for _, kp in ipairs(seq.Keypoints) do
		local v = kp.Value
		local base = tscale > 1 and (1 - v) or -v
		local scaled = math.clamp(v + base * offset, 0, 1)
		kps[#kps + 1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(kp.Time, scaled, kp.Envelope)
	end
	return NumberSequence.new(kps)
end

-- Ramps startVal to endVal by rampEnd, then holds endVal.
function Helpers.earlyRampSeq(startVal, endVal, rampEnd)
	rampEnd = math.clamp(rampEnd, 0, 1)
	if rampEnd <= 0 then return NumberSequence.new(endVal) end
	if rampEnd >= 1 then return Helpers.seq2(startVal, endVal) end
	return NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, startVal),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(rampEnd, endVal),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, endVal),
	})
end

-- startVal to midVal by tMid, held until tEndStart, then to endVal at 1.
function Helpers.threeStageSeq(startVal, midVal, endVal, tMid, tEndStart)
	tMid = math.clamp(tMid, 0, 1)
	tEndStart = math.clamp(tEndStart, tMid, 1)
	local kps = { NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, startVal) }
	if tMid > 0 and tMid < 1 then kps[#kps + 1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(tMid, midVal) end
	if tEndStart > tMid and tEndStart < 1 then
		kps[#kps + 1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(tEndStart, midVal)
	end
	kps[#kps + 1] = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, endVal)
	return NumberSequence.new(kps)
end

-- ColorSequenceKeypoint rejects components above 1, which Forge's HDR colours carry.
function Helpers.clampColor(c)
	if typeof(c) ~= "Color3" then return Color3.new(1, 1, 1) end
	return Color3.new(
		math.clamp(c.R, 0, 1),
		math.clamp(c.G, 0, 1),
		math.clamp(c.B, 0, 1)
	)
end

function Helpers.colorSeq2(startC, endC)
	startC = Helpers.clampColor(startC or Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
	endC = Helpers.clampColor(endC or startC)
	return ColorSequence.new({
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, startC),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, endC),
	})
end

-- Forge EffectDuration (NumberRange) or Duration, as a Lifetime range.
function Helpers.readDuration(model)
	local effDur = model:GetAttribute("EffectDuration")
	if typeof(effDur) == "NumberRange" then return effDur end
	local legacy = model:GetAttribute("Duration")
	if typeof(legacy) == "number" then return NumberRange.new(legacy) end
	if typeof(legacy) == "NumberRange" then return legacy end
	return NumberRange.new(1)
end

-- The NormalId whose axis in sourceCFrame's frame is closest to worldDir.
local _AXIS_TABLE = {
	{Enum.NormalId.Top,    Vector3.new(0,  1,  0)},
	{Enum.NormalId.Bottom, Vector3.new(0, -1,  0)},
	{Enum.NormalId.Right,  Vector3.new(1,  0,  0)},
	{Enum.NormalId.Left,   Vector3.new(-1, 0,  0)},
	{Enum.NormalId.Back,   Vector3.new(0,  0,  1)},
	{Enum.NormalId.Front,  Vector3.new(0,  0, -1)},
}
function Helpers.closestEmissionDirection(sourceCFrame, worldDir)
	local localDir = sourceCFrame:VectorToObjectSpace(worldDir)
	local best, bestDot = Enum.NormalId.Top, -math.huge
	for _, t in ipairs(_AXIS_TABLE) do
		local d = localDir:Dot(t[2])
		if d > bestDot then bestDot = d; best = t[1] end
	end
	return best
end

-- YXZ Euler degrees, which RotOrder Global (Ry * Rx * Rz) composes back. YXZ aliases past 90 degrees
-- on X, which breaks tweening; tweenableEulerDeg avoids that for single-axis turns.
function Helpers.eulerDegYXZ(cf)
	local rx, ry, rz = cf:ToEulerAnglesYXZ()
	return math.deg(rx), math.deg(ry), math.deg(rz)
end

-- Axis and angle in degrees by the trace formula; identity gives ((1, 0, 0), 0). Degenerate at 180 degrees.
function Helpers.axisAngle(rotCF)
	local _, _, _, R00, R01, R02, R10, R11, R12, R20, R21, R22 = rotCF:GetComponents()
	local trace = R00 + R11 + R22
	local cosTheta = math.clamp((trace - 1) * 0.5, -1, 1)
	local angle = math.acos(cosTheta)
	if math.abs(angle) < 1e-6 then return Vector3.new(1, 0, 0), 0 end
	local sinTheta = math.sin(angle)
	if math.abs(sinTheta) > 1e-6 then
		local ax = (R21 - R12) / (2 * sinTheta)
		local ay = (R02 - R20) / (2 * sinTheta)
		local az = (R10 - R01) / (2 * sinTheta)
		local axis = Vector3.new(ax, ay, az)
		if axis.Magnitude > 1e-6 then return axis.Unit, math.deg(angle) end
	end
	return Vector3.new(1, 0, 0), math.deg(angle)
end

-- Euler degrees that tween linearly from (0, 0, 0): a single-axis turn puts its whole signed angle
-- on that axis; a mixed turn falls back to eulerDegYXZ, which may alias.
function Helpers.tweenableEulerDeg(rotCF)
	local axis, angleDeg = Helpers.axisAngle(rotCF)
	if math.abs(angleDeg) < 1e-3 then return 0, 0, 0 end
	local ax, ay, az = math.abs(axis.X), math.abs(axis.Y), math.abs(axis.Z)
	local PURE_AXIS_TOLERANCE = 0.99
	if ax > PURE_AXIS_TOLERANCE then
		return math.sign(axis.X) * angleDeg, 0, 0
	end
	if ay > PURE_AXIS_TOLERANCE then
		return 0, math.sign(axis.Y) * angleDeg, 0
	end
	if az > PURE_AXIS_TOLERANCE then
		return 0, 0, math.sign(axis.Z) * angleDeg
	end
	return Helpers.eulerDegYXZ(rotCF)
end

-- Forge's FlipbookTextures buffer: one f64 asset id per frame.
function Helpers.deserializeFlipbook(data)
	if not data then return nil end
	local buf
	if typeof(data) == "string" then buf = buffer.fromstring(data)
	elseif typeof(data) == "buffer" then buf = data
	else return nil end
	local count = buffer.len(buf) / 8
	if count == 0 then return nil end
	local ids = {}
	for i = 0, count - 1 do
		table.insert(ids, buffer.readf64(buf, i * 8))
	end
	return ids
end

-- Part-Icles markers the converter writes once; every strip keeps them.
local _PERMANENT_KEEP = {
	_convertedByPartIcles = true,
	_isAnchor = true,
}

-- Attributes Transform writes. Stale copies on a Forge source make stripAllForge skip it and
-- Transform return early, leaving an empty wrapper.
local _PARTICLES_MARKERS = {
	"Transformed", "Qwinkle", "IsEmitter",
	"EmissionMode", "AnimateLoop",
	"PreloadTexture", "LinkMode", "LinkSource",
}

function Helpers.clearPartIclesMarkers(inst)
	for _, name in ipairs(_PARTICLES_MARKERS) do
		inst:SetAttribute(name, nil)
	end
end

-- Clears the attributes and tags of `inst` alone. For containers whose descendants were
-- already converted and carry emit attributes a subtree sweep would remove.
function Helpers.stripOwnForge(inst)
	for name in pairs(inst:GetAttributes()) do
		if not _PERMANENT_KEEP[name] then
			inst:SetAttribute(name, nil)
		end
	end
	for _, tag in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTags(inst)) do
		CollectionService:RemoveTag(inst, tag)
	end
end

-- Clears every attribute and tag under rootInst except Transformed subtrees and _PERMANENT_KEEP.
-- Converters read what they need first; Transform then writes fresh. Returns the counts.
function Helpers.stripAllForge(rootInst)
	local attrsStripped, tagsRemoved = 0, 0
	local function _visit(inst)
		-- A Transformed node and its subtree are Part-Icles content.
		if inst:GetAttribute("Transformed") then return end
		for name in pairs(inst:GetAttributes()) do
			if not _PERMANENT_KEEP[name] then
				inst:SetAttribute(name, nil)
				attrsStripped += 1
			end
		end
		for _, tag in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTags(inst)) do
			CollectionService:RemoveTag(inst, tag)
			tagsRemoved += 1
		end
		for _, child in ipairs(inst:GetChildren()) do _visit(child) end
	end
	_visit(rootInst)
	return attrsStripped, tagsRemoved
end

-- stripAllForge for an effect inside a RenderTemplate: keeps EmitCount / EmitDelay / EmitDuration,
-- which EnableEmitSingle reads to switch it on each emit, and turns this copy off (emit-time
-- clones are switched on).
function Helpers.stripPreservingNestedEmit(rootInst)
	local emitCount = rootInst:GetAttribute("EmitCount")
	local emitDelay = rootInst:GetAttribute("EmitDelay")
	local emitDuration = rootInst:GetAttribute("EmitDuration")
	Helpers.stripAllForge(rootInst)
	if emitCount ~= nil then rootInst:SetAttribute("EmitCount", emitCount) end
	if emitDelay ~= nil then rootInst:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", emitDelay) end
	if emitDuration ~= nil then rootInst:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", emitDuration) end
	if rootInst:IsA("Trail") or rootInst:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then
		-- No EmitDuration: the Trail runs for the particle's whole life.
		if rootInst:GetAttribute("EmitDuration") == nil and rootInst:IsA("Trail") then
			rootInst:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", math.huge)
		end
		pcall(function() rootInst.Enabled = false end)
	end
	-- A Beam or a Light it is or holds goes off too, marked so every emit-time clone has it on.
	AtRest.silenceHeld(rootInst)
end

-- Converts a Forge EmitOnFinish / EmitOnImpact folder into a hidden Folder on the clone and arms
-- `eventName` with EmitMode AtPosition and EmitTarget at that folder. ctx.walkForgeSubtree comes
-- from init.luau. Returns true when armed.
function Helpers.wireEmitTarget(ctx, clone, sourceContainer, report, srcChildName, eventName, outFolderName, srcLabel)
	local src = sourceContainer:FindFirstChild(srcChildName)
	if not src or #src:GetChildren() == 0 then return false end
	if not ctx.walkForgeSubtree then return false end
	local targetFolder = Instance.new("Folder")
	targetFolder.Name = outFolderName
	targetFolder.Parent = clone
	ctx.walkForgeSubtree(src, targetFolder)
	if #targetFolder:GetChildren() == 0 then
		targetFolder:Destroy()
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format(
			"%s  -  %s folder had %d children but none were convertible to Part-Icles emitters.",
			srcLabel or sourceContainer.Name, srcChildName, #src:GetChildren())
		return false
	end
	local cfg = EventsSchema.ensureEvent(clone, eventName)
	if not cfg then
		targetFolder:Destroy()
		report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format(
			"%s  -  %s present but %s event is invalid for this emitter type.",
			srcLabel or sourceContainer.Name, srcChildName, eventName)
		return false
	end
	cfg:SetAttribute("Enabled", true)
	cfg:SetAttribute("EmitMode", "AtPosition")
	local et = cfg:FindFirstChild("EmitTarget")
	if et and et:IsA("ObjectValue") then
		et.Value = targetFolder
	end
	return true
end

return Helpers

--[[
	LightningConverter: turns a Forge LightningBolt (an Attachment tagged "LightningBolt" holding a
	template Part and a `Points` bezier path) into a Part-Icles Lightning emitter.
	  path      The chord from Forge's emission frame to the path end. With an `End` attachment
	            the bolt runs to a child Attachment at that point (TargetMode Point); without one
	            it fires along the chord for its length (Directional). One bend becomes Sag.
	  timeline  Lifetime = Duration + DestroyDelay + dissipation. The head sweep becomes
	            GrowthSpeed; the Width / Transparency tweens, both fades and the Scale dissipation
	            are baked into the Thickness and Transparency graphs (LightningTimeline).
	  shape     Segments, Jaggedness x OffsetScale -> Amplitude, RefreshRate -> JitterRate.
	  spawn     A BasePart parent scatters bolt starts inside its box (PosX/Y/Z, world axes).
	Not mapped, each reported: a travelling window (Length below 1), projectile flight, the Fill
	highlight, Head / Tail nested effects, speed scaling.

	The emitter replaces the source Attachment under the same parent. Cross-file: `IsLightning` is
	stamped after the attribute strip and before Transform (Modules/Part/Transform reads it).

	API: convert(ctx, sourceAttachment, report)
]]

local Helpers = require(script.Parent.Helpers)
local CurveSampling = require(script.Parent.CurveSampling)
local BezierConverter = require(script.Parent.BezierConverter)
local Timeline = require(script.Parent.LightningTimeline)

local LightningConverter = {}

local PATH_SAMPLES = 24
local MIN_CHORD = 0.05
local MAX_SEGMENTS = 64
-- A bend shallower than this fraction of the chord converts as a straight bolt.
local MIN_SAG = 0.01

local function addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, message)
	report.warnings[#report.warnings + 1] = string.format("Lightning '%s': %s", sourceAttachment.Name, message)
end

local function normalIdOf(value)
	if typeof(value) == "EnumItem" then return value end
	local ok, item = pcall(function() return Enum.NormalId[value] end)
	if ok and item then return item end
	return Enum.NormalId.Top
end

-- The parent Forge reads the origin from. A directly selected attachment sits under a wrapper
-- Model and carries its real parent in the `_OrigForgeParent` sidecar (ForgeConverter/init).
local function originParentOf(sourceAttachment)
	local sidecar = sourceAttachment:FindFirstChild("_OrigForgeParent")
	if sidecar and sidecar:IsA("ObjectValue") and sidecar.Value then return sidecar.Value end
	return sourceAttachment.Parent
end

-- World CFrame of the lightning attachment, built from intrinsic CFrames so it also holds
-- under the wrapper Model.
local function attachmentWorldCFrame(sourceAttachment, parent)
	if parent and parent:IsA("BasePart") then return parent.CFrame * sourceAttachment.CFrame end
	if parent and parent:IsA("Attachment") then return parent.WorldCFrame * sourceAttachment.CFrame end
	return sourceAttachment.WorldCFrame
end

-- Forge's emission frame without the per-bolt randomness: the frame the path is laid out in, at
-- the centre of the parent.
local function emissionFrame(sourceAttachment, parent)
	local normal = Vector3.FromNormalId(normalIdOf(Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "EmissionDirection", "Top")))
	local frame
	if parent and parent:IsA("BasePart") then
		local up = math.abs(normal:Dot(Vector3.yAxis)) > 0.99 and Vector3.zAxis or Vector3.yAxis
		frame = parent.CFrame * CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.zero, normal, up)
	else
		local origin = attachmentWorldCFrame(sourceAttachment, parent)
		if parent and parent:IsA("Attachment") then origin = parent.WorldCFrame end
		frame = origin * CFrame.new(Vector3.zero, normal).Rotation
	end
	if Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "ShapeFace", "Outward") == "Inward" then
		frame *= CFrame.fromOrientation(0, math.pi, 0)
	end
	return frame
end

-- World-space samples along the path. Returns (samples, hasEnd) or nil when there is no path.
local function samplePath(sourceAttachment, parent, frame)
	local localPoints = BezierConverter.buildPointsLocal(sourceAttachment, true)
	if not localPoints or #localPoints < 4 then return nil end

	local worldPoints = table.create(#localPoints)
	for index, point in ipairs(localPoints) do
		worldPoints[index] = frame * (point - localPoints[1])
	end

	local endAttachment = sourceAttachment:FindFirstChild("End")
	local hasEnd = endAttachment ~= nil and endAttachment:IsA("Attachment")
	if hasEnd then
		local attachmentCF = attachmentWorldCFrame(sourceAttachment, parent)
		local endWorld = attachmentCF * endAttachment.CFrame.Position
		local handle = endAttachment:FindFirstChild("T1")
		local handleWorld = endWorld
		if handle and handle:IsA("Attachment") then
			handleWorld = attachmentCF * (endAttachment.CFrame * handle.CFrame.Position)
		end
		worldPoints[#worldPoints] = endWorld
		worldPoints[#worldPoints - 1] = handleWorld
	end

	local samples = CurveSampling.sample3DBezier(worldPoints, PATH_SAMPLES, nil, nil, true)
	return samples, hasEnd
end

-- Chord, arc length and the largest sideways deviation of the sampled path.
local function measurePath(samples)
	local startPos = samples[1]
	local chord = samples[#samples] - startPos
	local chordLength = chord.Magnitude
	if chordLength < MIN_CHORD then return nil end

	local chordDir = chord.Unit
	local bend = Vector3.zero
	local opposite = 0
	local pathLength = 0
	for index = 2, #samples do
		pathLength += (samples[index] - samples[index - 1]).Magnitude
		local relative = samples[index] - startPos
		local sideways = relative - chordDir * relative:Dot(chordDir)
		if sideways.Magnitude > bend.Magnitude then bend = sideways end
	end
	if bend.Magnitude > 0 then
		for index = 2, #samples do
			local relative = samples[index] - startPos
			opposite = math.max(opposite, -relative:Dot(bend.Unit))
		end
	end
	return {
		startPos = startPos,
		endPos = samples[#samples],
		chordDir = chordDir,
		chordLength = chordLength,
		pathLength = pathLength,
		bend = bend,
		-- An S-shaped path swings to both sides of the chord; one Sag arc cannot follow it.
		isSCurve = bend.Magnitude > 0 and opposite > bend.Magnitude * 0.25,
	}
end

-- Emitter pose: LookVector along the chord, and the bend pointing along its -Y so Sag
-- (DisplacementMode RigidLocal droops along the emitter's -Y) reproduces the curve.
local function emitterCFrame(path, sag)
	local up
	if sag > 0 then
		up = -path.bend.Unit
	elseif math.abs(path.chordDir:Dot(Vector3.yAxis)) > 0.99 then
		up = Vector3.xAxis
	else
		up = Vector3.yAxis
	end
	return CFrame.lookAt(path.startPos, path.endPos, up)
end

-- Half extents of the parent's box along the world axes (bolt starts scatter inside it).
local function worldHalfExtents(part)
	local half = part.Size / 2
	local cf = part.CFrame
	local right, up, look = cf.RightVector, cf.UpVector, cf.LookVector
	return Vector3.new(
		math.abs(right.X) * half.X + math.abs(up.X) * half.Y + math.abs(look.X) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Y) * half.X + math.abs(up.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(look.Y) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Z) * half.X + math.abs(up.Z) * half.Y + math.abs(look.Z) * half.Z
	)
end

-- Builds the emitter Part from the template and transforms it. Returns (emitter, survivors).
local function buildEmitter(ctx, sourceAttachment, template, pose, keepChildren)
	local emitter = template:Clone()
	emitter.Name = sourceAttachment.Name
	emitter.Anchored = true
	emitter.CanCollide = false
	emitter.CanQuery = false
	emitter.CanTouch = false
	emitter.CFrame = pose

	-- Transform's RenderTemplate strip destroys bare emitters and lights; they are set aside
	-- and re-parented into the RenderTemplate afterwards. Forge copies the template's children
	-- onto segments only for NestedEffectMode All.
	local survivors = {}
	for _, child in ipairs(emitter:GetChildren()) do
		local isNestedEffect = child:IsA("ParticleEmitter") or child:IsA("Trail") or child:IsA("Light")
		if keepChildren and isNestedEffect then
			table.insert(survivors, child)
			child.Parent = nil
		elseif not keepChildren or child.Name == "EmitOnFinish" then
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end

	-- Own attributes only: kept children carry the emit attributes convertParticle stamped.
	Helpers.clearPartIclesMarkers(emitter)
	Helpers.stripOwnForge(emitter)
	emitter:SetAttribute("IsLightning", true)
	emitter.Parent = sourceAttachment.Parent or workspace

	local ok, err = pcall(function() ctx.Part:Transform(emitter) end)
	if not ok or not emitter:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
		emitter:Destroy()
		for _, child in ipairs(survivors) do child:Destroy() end
		return nil, tostring(err)
	end

	local renderTemplate = emitter:FindFirstChild("RenderTemplate")
	for _, child in ipairs(survivors) do
		if renderTemplate then
			Helpers.stripPreservingNestedEmit(child)
			child.Parent = renderTemplate
		else
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end
	return emitter
end

local function writeShape(TR, emitter, sourceAttachment, path, sag)
	local segments = math.clamp(math.floor(Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Segments", 8)), 2, MAX_SEGMENTS)
	local jaggedness = Helpers.range(sourceAttachment, "Jaggedness", 0.5, 1)
	local offsetScale = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "OffsetScale", 1)
	-- Forge offsets each interior point by jaggedness x OffsetScale x segment length, capped at
	-- 0.8 of it. Amplitude is a fraction of the whole bolt, so divide by the segment count; a
	-- decay of 1 keeps every subdivision level at that size, like Forge's per-point jitter.
	local amplitudeMin = math.min(jaggedness.Min * offsetScale, 0.8) / segments
	local amplitudeMax = math.min(jaggedness.Max * offsetScale, 0.8) / segments
	local refreshRate = math.max(Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "RefreshRate", 15), 0)

	TR.write(emitter, "SegmentCount", NumberRange.new(segments))
	TR.write(emitter, "Amplitude", NumberRange.new(math.min(amplitudeMin, amplitudeMax), math.max(amplitudeMin, amplitudeMax)))
	TR.write(emitter, "AmplitudeDecay", NumberRange.new(1))
	TR.write(emitter, "JitterRate", NumberRange.new(refreshRate))
	TR.write(emitter, "ShapeMode", "Jitter")
	TR.write(emitter, "Sag", NumberRange.new(sag))
	TR.write(emitter, "SagShape", NumberRange.new(1))
	TR.write(emitter, "DisplacementMode", "RigidLocal")
	TR.write(emitter, "EmissionDirection", Enum.NormalId.Front)
	TR.write(emitter, "Length", NumberRange.new(path.chordLength))
end

local function writeSpawn(TR, emitter, sourceAttachment, parent, hasEnd, report)
	local spread = sourceAttachment:GetAttribute("SpreadAngle")
	if typeof(spread) == "Vector3" and spread ~= Vector3.zero then
		if hasEnd then
			addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "SpreadAngle is not applied to a bolt that ends on an End attachment.")
		else
			TR.write(emitter, "SpreadAngle", Vector2.new(spread.Y, spread.X))
			addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "SpreadAngle converted as a cone around the bolt direction (approximate).")
		end
	end

	if not (parent and parent:IsA("BasePart")) then return end
	local half = worldHalfExtents(parent)
	if half.Magnitude < 0.05 then return end
	TR.write(emitter, "PosMode", "Global")
	TR.write(emitter, "PosX", NumberRange.new(-half.X, half.X))
	TR.write(emitter, "PosY", NumberRange.new(-half.Y, half.Y))
	TR.write(emitter, "PosZ", NumberRange.new(-half.Z, half.Z))
	local shape = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Shape", "Box")
	local style = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "ShapeStyle", "Volume")
	if shape ~= "Box" or style ~= "Volume" then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, string.format("spawn shape %s / %s converted as a box volume around the parent.", tostring(shape), tostring(style)))
	end
end

local function reportUnmapped(sourceAttachment, path, report)
	local lengthStart = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Length_Start", 1)
	local lengthEnd = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Length_End", 1)
	if lengthStart < 1 or lengthEnd < 1 then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "Length below 1 (a short bolt travelling along the path) converted as a full-length bolt.")
	end
	if sourceAttachment:GetAttribute("ProjectileEnabled") == true then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "projectile flight after the path is not converted.")
	end
	local fillStart = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Fill_Transparency_Start", 1)
	local fillEnd = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Fill_Transparency_End", 1)
	if fillStart < 1 or fillEnd < 1 then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "the Fill highlight is not converted.")
	end
	local speedStart = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Speed_Start", 1)
	local speedEnd = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Speed_End", 1)
	if speedStart ~= 1 or speedEnd ~= 1 then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "Speed_Start / Speed_End time scaling is not converted.")
	end
	if path.isSCurve then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "the path bends both ways; converted as a single arc.")
	end
end

function LightningConverter.convert(ctx, sourceAttachment, report)
	local template = sourceAttachment:FindFirstChildOfClass("Part")
	if not (sourceAttachment:IsA("Attachment") and template) then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "needs to be an Attachment with a template Part; skipped.")
		report.skippedCount += 1
		sourceAttachment:Destroy()
		return
	end

	local parent = originParentOf(sourceAttachment)
	local samples, hasEnd = samplePath(sourceAttachment, parent, emissionFrame(sourceAttachment, parent))
	local path = samples and measurePath(samples)
	if not path then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "has no usable Points path (two anchors, start and end apart); skipped.")
		report.skippedCount += 1
		sourceAttachment:Destroy()
		return
	end

	local sag = path.bend.Magnitude / path.chordLength
	if sag < MIN_SAG then sag = 0 end

	local nestedMode = Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "NestedEffectMode", "None")
	local emitter, transformError = buildEmitter(ctx, sourceAttachment, template, emitterCFrame(path, sag), nestedMode == "All")
	if not emitter then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "Transform failed (" .. tostring(transformError) .. "); skipped.")
		report.skippedCount += 1
		sourceAttachment:Destroy()
		return
	end

	local TR = ctx.TypeRegistry
	local timeline = Timeline.read(sourceAttachment)
	TR.write(emitter, "Lifetime", timeline.lifetime)
	TR.write(emitter, "Thickness", Timeline.thickness(timeline))
	TR.write(emitter, "Transparency", Timeline.transparency(timeline))
	TR.write(emitter, "Color", Timeline.color(timeline, template.Color))
	TR.write(emitter, "GrowthSpeed", NumberRange.new(timeline.duration > 0.02 and path.pathLength / timeline.duration or 0))
	TR.write(emitter, "Rate", Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "Rate", 5))

	writeShape(TR, emitter, sourceAttachment, path, sag)
	writeSpawn(TR, emitter, sourceAttachment, parent, hasEnd, report)

	if hasEnd then
		local marker = Instance.new("Attachment")
		marker.Name = "BoltEnd"
		marker.Parent = emitter
		marker.WorldPosition = path.endPos
		local target = emitter:FindFirstChild("Target")
		if target and target:IsA("ObjectValue") then target.Value = marker end
		TR.write(emitter, "TargetMode", "Point")
	else
		TR.write(emitter, "TargetMode", "Directional")
	end

	emitter:SetAttribute("EmitCount", Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "EmitCount", 1))
	emitter:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "EmitDelay", 0))
	emitter:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", Helpers.attr(sourceAttachment, "EmitDuration", 0))

	if nestedMode == "Head" or nestedMode == "Tail" then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "NestedEffectMode " .. nestedMode .. " (effects on one segment) is not converted.")
	elseif nestedMode == "All" then
		Helpers.wireEmitTarget(ctx, emitter, template, report, "EmitOnFinish", "OnDeath", "_OnDeath_EmitTargets", "Lightning '" .. sourceAttachment.Name .. "'")
	end
	if timeline.retractAsFade then
		addWarning(report, sourceAttachment, "Retract dissipation converted as a fade-out.")
	end
	reportUnmapped(sourceAttachment, path, report)

	sourceAttachment:Destroy()
	report.successCount += 1
	report.mappedTypes.lightning = (report.mappedTypes.lightning or 0) + 1
end

return LightningConverter
